       Leif Allred and Dr. Laura Pressley, pro se intervenors, file these Exceptions to the Proposal

for Decision ("PFD") filed by the presiding State Office of Administrative Hearings ("SOAH")

Administrative Law Judges ("ALJ") in this case concerning Oncor Electric Delivery Company

LLC's ("Oncor") and LCRA Transmission Service Corporation (“LCRA”) Joint Application to

Amend its Certificate of Convenience and Necessity for the Bell County East Switch to Big Hill

Substation 765-kV Transmission Line Project in Bell, Burnet, Concho, Coryell, Lampasas, Llano,

Mason, McCulloch, Menard, Milam, Mills, San Saba, Schleicher, Tom Green and Williamson

counties. Exceptions are presented infra.

                              I. Notice of Public Meeting
           Lack of Due Process and Equal Protection for Affected Land Owners
 1.       The Administrative Law Judges’ (ALJ’s) correctly find that Oncor failed to comply with

the notice requirements of Texas Administrative Code 22.52(a)(4)1 for roughly 1,400 landowners.

2.       Pro se intervenors, Allred and Pressley, respectfully request the Findings of Fact and

Conclusions of Law be augmented to explicitly state “roughly 1,400 land owners that were added

after the June 2025 meetings did not receive due process and equal treatment under federal and state

law.    Oncor violated the Fourteenth Amendment of the U.S. Constitituion and the Texas

Constitution Art. 1 Section 3, which both provide the state shall not deny any person within its

jurisdiction the equal protection of its state laws.”


                                   II. Prudent Avoidance
       Oncor Agreed to Design 765 kV Towers To Maximize Cancelling Effects of EMF’s

3.       The ALJ’s appropriately defined prudent avoidance as “[t]he limiting of exposures to

electric and magnetic fields (EMFs) that can be avoided with reasonable investments of money and

effort.”2 In their testimony in 2024, Oncor agreed to limit “reduce” exposures to EMFs for the

introduction of extra high voltage transmission line (765 kV) buildouts in the ERCOT market by:

         “designing [500 and 765 kV] transmission lines in a manner that maximizes the
         cancelling effects of the fields of adjacent phases of the transmission line, thereby
         reducing the strength of EMF’s.”3

above and Texas’ statutory requirements of prudent avoidance in 16 TAC § 25.101(a)(7) and

community values in Tex. Utilities Code § 37.056(c)(4)(A). All of which fall squarely within what

Texas legally requires and what Oncor has already agree to do and is now legally bound to do, to

design their 765 kV transmission lines that cancel and reduce the strengths of EMFs.

11.      We and the ALJ’s are not informed as to why Oncor failed in their Joint Amended

Application to propose 765 kV transmission lines designed to maximize the cancelling effects of

EMF’s and instead they chose a horizontal tangent design that performs the worst for EMF

emissions.16

12.      Because Oncor agreed to and has a legal responsibility to employ these reasonable prudent

avoidance measures, the Administrative Law Judges must hold them to their statutory responsibilit y

to utilizing transmission line designs with cancelling effects.

13.      We therefore request the ALJ’s augment their Findings of Fact and Conclusions of law that

because Oncor did not employ reasonable prudent avoidance measures of utilizing Delta tower

designs that utilize cancelling effects of EMFs, Oncor violated prudent avoidance measures of 16

TAC § 25.101(a)(7) which they were statutorily bound to employ because of their legally binding

testimony in PUC Case 55249-9, and their legal requirement to honor community values in Tex.

Utilities Code § 37.056(c)(4)(A) to reduce EMF’s.

14.      We request that the ALJ’s and PUC require the use of Delta designs for any 765 kV line
